app.name: ShailSuraksha
app.tagline: Landslide early warning for the eight North Eastern states
app.ministry: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region, Government of India

severityAction.green: No action needed. Stay aware during heavy rain.
severityAction.yellow: Stay alert. Avoid slopes and cut sections after dark.
severityAction.orange: Prepare to move. Keep documents and medicines ready.
severityAction.red: Leave now. Go to the nearest shelter by the marked route.

landing.eyebrow: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region · SIH26001
landing.headline: Warning at the scale of a single slope
landing.subhead: The rainfall data already exists. ShailSuraksha turns it into an explained, acknowledged warning for the village standing below the slope, in a language they read, on a phone with two bars of signal.
landing.terrainCaption: Live terrain. Elevation from AWS Terrain Tiles, basemap from CARTO.
landing.problemHeading: The data was never the missing piece
landing.problemBody: In June 2022 a slope above a railway construction site at Tupul, Manipur failed and buried a Territorial Army camp. The rainfall had been measured. The satellites had passed overhead. Nobody had turned any of it into a warning for that slope, for that village, in that language.
landing.statTupulLabel: Killed at Tupul and Noney, Manipur, June 2022
landing.statAizawlLabel: Killed in Aizawl, Mizoram, in a single day, May 2024
landing.gapHeading: Rainfall is measured nationally. Slopes fail locally.
landing.gapBody: The Geological Survey of India forecasts at district scale, and it forecasts well. A district is roughly the size of a small country's province. The slope that kills you is a few hundred metres across. ShailSuraksha works at that scale, explains every number it produces, and carries the result to the person standing on the slope.
landing.engineHeading: Four layers, every one of them inspectable
landing.engineBody: A single black-box classifier is what a hackathon usually produces. It cannot answer the only question that matters to a geologist, which is why. So we run four models and show all of them.
landing.layerPhysicsDetail: Infinite-slope factor of safety with transient pore pressure. Needs no training data and cannot overfit.
landing.layerEmpiricalDetail: Regional rainfall intensity and duration thresholds, antecedent precipitation, soil water index.
landing.layerMlDetail: Gradient-boosted susceptibility plus a temporal network over 30 days, calibrated so 70 per cent means 70 per cent.
landing.layerDeformationDetail: Satellite change detection and inverse-velocity failure timing from tiltmeters and extensometers.
landing.architectureBody: Every arrow records provenance. A risk score on screen can be walked back through the fusion, to its three component layers, to the features, to the source record and the moment it was fetched.
landing.dashboardsHeading: Five dashboards and a public portal
landing.d1Detail: 3D terrain command centre with extruded risk prisms, a time scrubber and click-to-explain.
landing.d2Detail: Which villages get cut off, which hospitals lose their catchment, and which five roads to clear first.
landing.d3Detail: Drag a rainfall slider and watch the risk surface recompute across the region.
landing.d4Detail: A transparent, tunable index over exposed population, vulnerable groups and access time.
landing.d5Detail: Geotagged photo reports classified on the phone itself, verified against their own EXIF data.
landing.d6Detail: Am I safe right now. No login, ten languages, works with the network switched off.
landing.honestyBody: Every figure in the interface carries its provenance. Green means the source answered just now. Amber means it came from cache, and shows its age. Blue means the seeded simulator produced it. There is no code path that strips that label, because a system that dresses up simulated data as live has no business issuing an evacuation order.
landing.honestyProbed: Data sources probed from the build machine, not assumed
landing.honestyContrast: Colour pairs measured against WCAG AA
landing.capHeading: Every alert is Common Alerting Protocol v1.2
landing.capBody: The same standard the NDMA SACHET pipeline consumes, and the same standard any state disaster authority already integrates with. This plugs into the national alerting stack rather than competing with it. Alerts require acknowledgement, unacknowledged high-tier alerts escalate up the hierarchy on a timer, and every issuance, suppression and override is written to an immutable audit log.
landing.footerNote: Built for Smart India Hackathon 2026, problem statement SIH26001.
landing.mapNote: 14,714 slope units from real elevation data

home.heading: The foundation is in place
home.intro: ShailSuraksha translates rainfall into a slope-scale, village-scale warning that reaches the right person, in a language they read, on a phone with two bars of signal.
home.notLiveYet: No risk model has been trained yet. Nothing on this page is a forecast, and no number here describes real hazard.

built.monorepo: Monorepo across web, api, ml, ingest, infra and docs
built.docs: Architecture, data sources and model card, written before any model
built.stack: Docker Compose for the full local stack, with CI on every push
built.tokens: Design tokens verified against WCAG AA, 76 pairs measured
built.i18n: Ten languages wired end to end, with honest fallback

home.sourcesNote: Each source below was contacted from the build machine. Status reflects what actually answered.
home.next: Phase 1 builds the geospatial foundation: the admin hierarchy, the terrain derivatives from the Copernicus 30 m digital elevation model, and hydrological slope units for the region.

footer.disclaimer: A decision-support tool. Not a substitute for official warnings from the Geological Survey of India or the India Meteorological Department.
